answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation, then slash that stake when independently sampled tasks expose duplicated or coordinated behavior. A fresh Sybil account starts with no history, so it cannot cheaply inherit trust; splitting capital among copper, quill, and canyon personas also divides voting weight and rewards while multiplying the stake at risk. The attacker pays upfront capital and loses it on detection, while honest agents build reputation through costly, repeated work.
